sections.h2: Which route gets a Stow house sold with the least friction?
sections.html:
Pick the route that fits the problem. A tidy Stow house can ride the open market, but one with a failing roof, a stubborn tenant or an unsettled estate may suit a buyer who accepts it unrepaired.

  • Agent listing: photography, open houses, the buyer's inspection and any repair requests that follow.
  • Owner-sold: you choose the price and take on the disclosure form and deed work yourself.
  • Direct cash sale: one buyer, one walkthrough, and a quicker trip to the county transfer desk.

All three finish with a deed filed through the county, so a title company or attorney should be on board from the start.

sections.h2: What is Stow like as a place to sell?
sections.html:
Stow is an Akron suburb on the Summit and Portage county line. Joshua Stow, a Connecticut native who never lived here, bought the 25-square-mile township in the Western Reserve survey. William Walker arrived as the first settler in 1802, and the township joined the new Summit County in 1840. Cuyahoga Falls, Munroe Falls and Silver Lake were later carved from its land, and what remained became a village in 1957.

Kent sits to the east, Tallmadge and Munroe Falls to the south, Hudson to the north and Cuyahoga Falls to the west, and shoppers tend to compare every one of them. The city covers 17.09 square miles of land and 0.23 of water.

Summers run warm and muggy and winters run cold. Stow is outside the main Lake Erie snowbelt but inside the secondary snowbelt, so heavier lake-effect snow shows up when the wind runs a certain way. An inspector will likely dwell on the roof, gutters, furnace and basement.

Three state routes serve the city: Ohio 8, Ohio 59 along Kent Road and Ohio 91 along Darrow Road. METRO RTA and PARTA buses stop in Stow, and Kent State University Airport is also located here.

sections.h2: Who is buying and living in Stow houses?
sections.html:
Stow's median age at the 2020 census was 41.6. Seniors made up 19.7 percent of the population, children under 18 made up 20.0 percent, and about three in ten of the 14,608 households were someone living alone.

QuickFacts reports a bachelor's degree or more for 48.0 percent of adults, plus a mean commute of 23.5 minutes and a poverty rate of 5.2 percent. Highway access is therefore a fair talking point in a listing, since Ohio 8 runs through town.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks do Stow buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The Stow-Munroe Falls City School District covers Stow and most of Munroe Falls. Its elementary buildings are Echo Hills, Fishcreek, Highland, Indian Trail, Riverview and Woodland, followed by Lakeview Intermediate, Kimpton Middle and Stow-Munroe Falls High School. Holy Family School is the Catholic choice for first through eighth grade.

Outdoor space gives listings extra weight:

  • Adell Durbin Park, Meadowbrook Lake Park, Silver Springs Park and Oregon Trail Park.
  • Fox Den Golf Course, which the city owns, and Roses Run Country Club beside the Cuyahoga River.
  • The paved Bike and Hike trail from Summit County MetroParks, 33.5 miles long, running through Stow toward Brandywine Falls.

Ground was broken on April 12, 2026 for an amphitheater called The AMP, with a finish date planned for the end of that year.

sections.h2: Do Stow permits and inspections affect a sale?
sections.html:
Sometimes, through unfinished work. If a buyer's inspector notices a newer deck, furnace, roof or finished basement, expect a request to see the permit. Pull your records before listing and close out whatever is still open.

The Stow Building Department runs permits and construction inspections, and its online portal accepts forms, inspection requests and contractor registrations at any hour. A call in before 9 am gets same-day inspection, and electric and plumbing visits happen on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday mornings. The department's line is 330-689-2729. Engineering, which handles drawings and the public right-of-way side of projects, is reached at 330-689-2719.

Stow's building office does not issue sanitary sewer permits. Those come from the Summit County Department of Sanitary Services, 1180 S Main Street in Akron, so call them about any sewer lateral question before closing. The Ohio Board of Building Standards writes the state codes that the city enforces.

sections.h2: What happens at the Summit County Fiscal Office when a Stow deed transfers?
sections.html:
The Fiscal Office's Property Transfer Department checks the legal description and approves the conveyance. Every deed travels with a DTE 100 statement of value, or a DTE 100 (EX) when an exemption applies. Paperwork received by 3:30 PM can be approved that same day.

The Fiscal Office fee page prints three lines that matter at closing:

  • Conveyance Fee: $4.00 per $1000 rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price.
  • Lot Fee: 50 cents per lot contained in the legal description.
  • Basic recording: $34.00 for two pages, $8.00 for each additional page.

Under Ohio Revised Code 322.02 the county's transfer tax falls on the grantor, who pays the auditor at delivery of the deed. Have the closing agent check your settlement statement against these lines.

sections.h2: Which disclosure form applies to a Stow seller?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the state's property disclosure form for houses with up to four units. Hand each prospective buyer a signed, dated copy early, because a buyer who gets it late can rescind in writing. The form asks about water, sewer, structure and hazards such as radon and lead paint.

Fill in each item in good faith. Where you truly lack the facts, the statute allows a good-faith approximation.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer worth considering in Stow?
sections.html:
A direct purchase suits an estate house with deferred repairs, a rental with a tenant, or an owner who has moved away and is carrying two sets of bills. If a roof or sewer line is near the end of its life, an as-is buyer spares you the repair decision.

Compare any figure with the net from a listing after commission and repairs. Ask who covers the transfer charge, how long the title work runs and what happens if the buyer walks away, then get every answer in the contract.

faqs.q: Who pays the county transfer charge on a Stow sale?
faqs.a: You do, as the seller. Ohio Revised Code 322.02 puts the county transfer tax on the grantor, and the Summit County auditor side of the Fiscal Office takes payment when the deed comes in.

faqs.q: What inspections does the City of Stow perform?
faqs.a: Permit inspections on construction work, with same-day service for calls before 9 am. Check with the Building Department at 330-689-2729 about your address, and plan on the buyer ordering a private inspection.

faqs.q: Which office records a Stow deed?
faqs.a: A Stow address falls under Summit County, which means the Fiscal Office records the instrument after the transfer step. Ask for the per-page recording charge when you schedule the closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stow house that has a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand the buyer the lease and the deposit ledger, or set a vacate date in the contract. Landlord-tenant duties continue until the day title changes hands.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a house in Stow?
faqs.a: Start by learning who is legally allowed to sign. The probate court and the Fiscal Office can say which affidavit or certificate moves title out of the decedent's name, and an Ohio probate attorney can sort out the rest before you accept an offer.
